thinking_and_logic: You began with a nested-loop plan, correctly noticing it would be slow. After hints, you transitioned to the optimal approach: maintain a dictionary from previously seen value to its index; for each current value n at index i, compute complement = target - n and check whether it’s already in the dictionary, returning the stored index and i if so; otherwise store n -> i and continue. This matches the expected reasoning and avoids using the same element twice by checking before inserting.
code_assessment: Your final code matches the answer key’s optimal single-pass hash-map solution (seen value -> index, check complement before inserting). Compared to the brute-force canonical alternative, your approach achieves O(n) time instead of O(n^2) and correctly preserves original indices (unlike sort-based approaches). The main gap vs an ideal interview performance isn’t the implementation—it’s that the key technique (hash map + complement lookup) required multiple hints to surface.
